$comment: 01.7.1-T4.2 (AC6): vulnerability-scan allowlist consumed by scripts/audit-deps.sh. Keyed by advisory id (GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz or CVE-YYYY-NNNNN — the last path segment of the advisory URL from 'npm audit --json' or 'dotnet list package --vulnerable --format json'). Every entry must name the accepting ADR (adr), the affected package, and the reason; 'expires' (YYYY-MM-DD) is optional — an expired exception no longer exempts. 'scope' is optional and npm-only: {"npm": [{"workspace": "<workspace name>", "via": "<direct dependency>"}]} narrows the exemption to the assessed chains — every production path from a workspace root to the package (npm ls <package> --all --omit=dev --package-lock-only --workspaces --include-workspace-root) must start with one of the listed pairs, and a non-npm finding, a package mismatch, bad scope data, an npm ls failure or a path through the root package or another workspace fails the gate instead of being exempted. An empty object means no exceptions: every vulnerability found by the scanners fails the gate.

GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf.reason: No patched release exists (affected <=4.0.7, patched none; latest published 4.0.7). At the time of this decision the only --omit=dev chain is the web build/localization tooling via @angular/localize -> tinyglobby -> picomatch; nothing in the repository invokes the localization CLIs, and no browser, server or customer-side runtime path was found. Exploitation needs an attacker-controlled glob pattern, which only build configuration or a developer command could supply. The entry is chain-scoped below to that assessed chain: any other production dependent of picomatch fails the gate on every run, and the coordinator still re-checks on the expiry. Build-time risk accepted until 2026-12-18; ends early on a patched release or a new production chain that passes untrusted patterns.
